html:
Medea is a tragedy by Euripides, first staged in Athens in 431 BCE, the year the Peloponnesian War began.

Medea is a princess from Colchis, on the far shore of the Black Sea, who helped Jason and the Argonauts win the Golden Fleece and gave up her home for him. Now they live in Corinth, and Jason leaves her to marry the king's daughter. Medea takes revenge: she kills the new bride and the king with poisoned gifts, then kills her own two sons to leave Jason with nothing. She escapes in a chariot sent by her grandfather, the sun god.

The play came last in its contest. Yet it became one of the most performed Greek tragedies. Euripides gives Medea strong speeches about how women are treated, and he makes the audience understand her even as she does something monstrous. As a foreign woman in a Greek city, she also raises questions about outsiders that still feel current. Sophocles won the prize in many years when Euripides did not.
sum: Medea is a tragedy by Euripides, first staged in Athens in 431 BCE, the year the Peloponnesian War began.
